questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagents, [A] and [B] used up when Salicylic acid undergoes the following reactions:
questions.solution:
Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) contains both a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$) and a phenolic hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$).

In reaction [A], the $-\text{COOH}$ group is converted into an ester group ($-\text{COOCH}_3$), while the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group remains unaffected. This product is methyl salicylate (oil of wintergreen). This transformation is a Fischer esterification, which requires methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}^+$). Thus, reagent [A] is $\dfrac{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}{\text{H}^+}$.

In reaction [B], the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group is acetylated to form an ester ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$), while the $-\text{COOH}$ group remains unaffected. This product is acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin). This acetylation is typically carried out using acetic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}^+$) and gentle warming. Thus, reagent [B] is $\dfrac{(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}}{\text{H}^+(warm)}$.

Comparing this with the given options, option (C) correctly identifies both reagents.

Answer: A: $\dfrac{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}{\text{H}^+}$ B: $\dfrac{(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}}{\text{H}^+(warm)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Acetic acid does not reduce Fehling's solution
Acetic acid gives effervescence with aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$ solution
Acetic acid on reaction with HI and red P at 473 K gives iodoethane
Acetic acid is a weaker acid than formic acid
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: Acetic acid lacks an aldehyde group, so it does not reduce Fehling's solution.

(2) Correct: Acetic acid reacts with $NaHCO_3$ releasing $CO_2$, causing effervescence:
$CH_3COOH + NaHCO_3 \to CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2\uparrow$

(3) Incorrect: Red P/HI reduces carboxylic acids all the way to the corresponding alkane, not a haloalkane. Acetic acid gives ethane, not iodoethane:
$CH_3COOH $\xrightarrow{Red\ P/HI,\ \Delta}$ CH_3CH_3$

(4) Correct: The $+I$ effect of the methyl group in acetic acid destabilises the acetate ion compared to the formate ion, making acetic acid a weaker acid than formic acid.

The incorrect statement is (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound [X] (Molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_2$ ) reacts with dil. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ to form an alcohol [B] and a carboxylic acid [C]. Reaction of compound $[\mathrm{B}]$ with Jones reagent yielded compound $[\mathrm{C}]$. When compound $[\mathrm{C}]$ was heated with $\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ an Anhydride was formed. Compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_2$ corresponds to an ester. Hydrolysis of an ester $\mathrm{RCOOR}'$ with dilute $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ yields a carboxylic acid $\mathrm{RCOOH}$ and an alcohol $\mathrm{R}'\mathrm{OH}$.

Given that the alcohol [B] is oxidized by Jones reagent to the carboxylic acid [C], it implies that the alcohol [B] and the acid [C] must contain the same number of carbon atoms. Since the total number of carbons in the ester is 6, the acid and the alcohol must each contain 3 carbons.

The acid [C] is propanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH}$) and the alcohol [B] is propan-1-ol ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$).

The ester [X] formed from propanoic acid and propan-1-ol is propyl propanoate, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COO} \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_3$.

Reviewing the provided options, option (ag53o) represents $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{COO} \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CH}_3$, which is propyl propanoate. Heating propanoic acid with $\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ yields propanoic anhydride, consistent with the problem statement.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{COO}-\left(\mathrm{CH}_2\right)_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following compounds, the most acidic is :
questions.solution:
The acidity of benzoic acid derivatives is determined by the electronic effects of the substituents present on the benzene ring.

The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) due to both its negative inductive effect ($-I$) and negative resonance effect ($-M$). The methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) is an electron-donating group (EDG) due to its positive resonance effect ($+M$), which outweighs its negative inductive effect ($-I$) at the para position.

Comparing the given compounds:
1. 4-methoxybenzoic acid: The $-OCH_3$ group decreases the acidity of benzoic acid by donating electron density into the ring.
2. Benzoic acid: This is the reference compound.
3. 4-nitrobenzoic acid: The $-NO_2$ group increases the acidity of benzoic acid significantly due to its strong electron-withdrawing nature.
4. 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid: This compound contains two $-NO_2$ groups. Both groups exert strong electron-withdrawing effects ($-I$ and $-M$). The presence of two such groups makes the carboxylate anion significantly more stable than in the case of 4-nitrobenzoic acid, thereby making 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid the most acidic among the choices.

Answer: 3, 4-dinitrobenzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A sweet smelling organic compound $[\mathrm{A}] \left(\mathrm{C}_9 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}_2\right)$ undergoes acid hydrolysis to form an acid [B].
Compound [B] further reacts with Ammonia followed by heating to yield [C].
Compound $[\mathrm{C}]$ when reacted with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ in caustic potash gave compound $[\mathrm{D}] \left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H} 7 \mathrm{~N}\right)$ which gives a white precipitate with aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$.
Identify compounds $[\mathrm{A}]$ & $[\mathrm{D}]$
questions.solution:
Compound [A] has the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_2$. Acid hydrolysis of [A] yields an acid [B]. Since [A] is a sweet-smelling ester, it is likely an ester of benzoic acid. Ethyl benzoate ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOCH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3$) has the formula $\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_2$.

Hydrolysis of ethyl benzoate gives benzoic acid [B] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOH}$) and ethanol. Benzoic acid reacts with ammonia to form ammonium benzoate, which upon heating yields benzamide [C] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CONH}_2$).

Compound [C] (benzamide) reacts with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ in caustic potash ($\mathrm{KOH}$), which is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This converts the amide group $-\mathrm{CONH}_2$ into an amine group $-\mathrm{NH}_2$, yielding aniline [D] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}_2$).

Aniline has the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_7\mathrm{N}$ and reacts with aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$ to form 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, which is a white precipitate. Thus, [A] is ethyl benzoate and [D] is aniline.

Answer: A: Ethyl benzoate D: Aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following correctly represents the decreasing order of acidic nature of the given carboxylic acids:
[A] 2-Hydroxybenzoic acid
[B] Benzoic acid
[C] 3-Hydroxybenzoic acid
[D] 4- Hydroxybenzoic acid
questions.solution:
The acidity of substituted benzoic acids is determined by the electronic effects of the substituents. The -OH group exerts both an electron-withdrawing inductive effect (-I) and an electron-donating resonance effect (+M).

In 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid), the ortho-effect and intramolecular hydrogen bonding significantly stabilize the conjugate base (carboxylate anion), making it the most acidic among the given compounds.

In 3-hydroxybenzoic acid, the -OH group is at the meta position. Resonance effects do not operate from the meta position, so only the -I effect of the -OH group acts, which increases acidity compared to benzoic acid.

In 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, the -OH group is at the para position. Here, the +M effect is dominant over the -I effect, which increases the electron density on the ring and destabilizes the carboxylate anion, making it less acidic than benzoic acid.

Benzoic acid serves as the reference. Comparing these, the order of acidity is 2-hydroxybenzoic acid > 3-hydroxybenzoic acid > benzoic acid > 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, which corresponds to [A] > [C] > [B] > [D].

Answer: $[\mathrm{A}]> [\mathrm{C}]> [\mathrm{B}]> [\mathrm{D}]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds would not be expected to decarboxylate when heated?
questions.solution:
Decarboxylation of carboxylic acids upon heating typically requires the presence of a carbonyl group at the $\beta$-position relative to the carboxyl group. This allows for the formation of a stable six-membered cyclic transition state involving the transfer of the carboxylic acid proton to the $\beta$-carbonyl oxygen, followed by the loss of carbon dioxide to form an enol, which then tautomerizes to a ketone.

Analyzing the given structures:
1. The first structure is 3-oxobutanoic acid (acetoacetic acid), which has a $\beta$-keto group and readily decarboxylates.
2. The second structure is propanedioic acid (malonic acid), which has a $\beta$-carboxyl group and readily decarboxylates.
3. The third structure is butanedioic acid (succinic acid). In this molecule, the carboxyl groups are at the $\gamma$-position relative to each other (separated by two methylene groups). There is no $\beta$-carbonyl or $\beta$-carboxyl group present to facilitate the cyclic transition state required for easy decarboxylation. Thus, it is stable towards decarboxylation under standard conditions.
4. The fourth structure is 3-oxopentanoic acid, which has a $\beta$-keto group and readily decarboxylates.

Therefore, butanedioic acid is the compound that would not be expected to decarboxylate easily.

Answer:
